title: Software Supply-Chain SBOM for Models: A 'Model Bill of Materials' to Audit Hidden Shared Dependencies

original_idea.body:
# Software Supply-Chain SBOM for Models

From public model cards and lineage metadata, construct dependency graphs for open models/derivatives, then behaviorally test whether models sharing an upstream dependency also share a vulnerability (same jailbreak works on all descendants). Metadata + light inference.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Level 4: strong chain — a Model-BOM maps and behaviorally tests shared dependencies, directly addressing the systemic-risk monitoring gap.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Level 4: build dependency graphs from metadata + behavioral transfer tests; metadata wrangling + scaffold add moderate complexity.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Level 4: focused deliverable (dependency graph + transitive-vulnerability test) but two-part adds dependencies.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Level 4: public metadata + open models, monitoring prototype labs underweight, no internal access.

low_compute.reasoning: Metadata analysis + light inference, low compute.

novelty.reasoning: A behaviorally-tested Model Bill of Materials appears largely novel.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: No known behaviorally-validated Model BOM for shared-dependency auditing.
